items.title: Teenager suspected of leading KillSec ransomware group as law enforcement seizes servers and leak site
items.summary: Law enforcement took control of the KillSec ransomware leak site on 30 September, seized servers and secured at least 110 TB of stolen data; a teenager is suspected of leading the group, Europol says.

items.title: 2026-014: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory: Citrix's 27 September bulletin fixes 8 flaws in customer-managed NetScaler ADC and Gateway, including 2 critical unauthenticated RCEs that Citrix confirms are actively exploited. Patch urgently.

items.title: Denmark Says Attackers Accessed CPR Data for 8.8 Million People via Company Account
items.summary: Denmark's digitalisation ministry says attackers used a private company's account to access names, addresses and personal ID numbers of about 8.8 million living and dead people in the national CPR register.

items.title: US, Australia warn of latest Citrix vulnerability after NetScaler advisory
items.summary: Citrix disclosed a third actively exploited NetScaler zero-day in under a week, CVE-2026-88779, a memory overflow causing denial of service; US and Australian agencies issued warnings. Impact seen as lower than the earlier pair.

items.title: Microsoft Exchange Flaw Lets Authenticated Attackers Read Other Users' Mailboxes
items.summary: Microsoft released out-of-band updates for CVE-2026-96940 (CVSS 8.8), an Exchange Server privilege escalation that lets authenticated attackers read other users' mailboxes.

items.title: 2026-013: Critical Vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP APM
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory: F5 fixed a critical vulnerability in BIG-IP APM on 22 September and confirms exploitation in the wild. CERT-EU recommends acting as soon as possible.

items.title: 2026-012: Critical Vulnerabilities in Check Point Products
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory: Check Point issued emergency updates on 9 September for two critical flaws in Security Gateway, Management Server and Spark Firewall deployments using Remote Access or Site-to-Site VPN.

items.title: OpenAI admits response to Australian government hacks 'not good enough'
items.summary: At a hearing, OpenAI executive Jason Kwon admitted the company's response to hacks of Australian government systems was 'not good enough' and said more precautions were added to its training environments.

items.title: ClickFix Smuggles Payloads Through Browser Cache to Bypass Windows Run Limits
items.summary: A new ClickFix variant uses compromised websites to pre-fetch a malicious script into the browser cache, then tricks users into executing the cached payload, sidestepping Windows Run dialog length limits.

items.title: EU mulls tougher restrictions on Russian diplomats as hybrid threats intensify
items.summary: After a spate of hybrid attacks across Europe, EU member states are considering tighter restrictions and checks on Russian diplomats over their possible involvement.

items.title: Atlassian warns of critical file access flaw in its datacenter products
items.summary: Atlassian warns of a critical file access vulnerability in its Data Center products and tells customers action is required.

items.title: South Korea's Lee says AI appears to have been used in bank hacks
items.summary: South Korean President Lee says AI appears to have been used in hacks against banks.

items.title: Security researcher claims they found KVM guest-host escape flaw
items.summary: A security researcher claims a KVM guest-to-host escape flaw, apparently affecting Firecracker microVMs that originated at AWS; relevant to multi-tenant virtualisation.

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: Accenture contractor removed from FBI following damaging data breach, sources say
items.summary: Reuters reports, citing sources, that an Accenture contractor was removed from FBI work following a damaging data breach.

items.title: ClingSTUN Turns Vulnerable IoT Devices Into Proxy Nodes
items.summary: ClingSTUN, a Linux backdoor, exploits 24 known flaws to compromise IoT devices, turns them into proxy nodes and hides communications via legitimate public STUN servers.

items.title: Alleged ShinyHunters member reportedly detained in Jordan, assisting law enforcement
items.summary: Alleged ShinyHunters member Saif al-Din Khader is reportedly detained in Jordan and cooperating with the FBI; the bureau confirms multiple arrests linked to the hack that exposed employee data.

items.title: Ukraine grocery chain ATB confirms cyberattack as hackers threaten to leak data
items.summary: Ukraine's largest grocery chain ATB confirmed a cyberattack after hackers posted an extortion demand on its website and threatened to leak data.

items.title: Chinese Hackers Impersonate US Officials for AI Cyber Espionage
items.summary: Emerging China-linked group TA419 impersonated US officials and built seemingly legitimate relationships with AI policy experts at think tanks, universities and law firms for espionage.

items.title: Thought for the week: AI agents raise new cybersecurity and liability questions
items.summary: IAPP weekly commentary on how autonomous AI agents create new cybersecurity exposure and unresolved liability questions for organisations deploying them.

items.title: Trump says 'threat' led US to pull bombers from RAF Fairford
items.summary: The Pentagon moved B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford back to US bases; Trump cited a 'threat', while reporting points to wider US frustration over UK defence spending.

items.title: Fake NATO deaths, Epstein claims and drones: how Russia targets elections in the Baltics
items.summary: A new report finds Russia-linked disinformation around Estonian and Latvian elections focused on sowing confusion about security issues, such as fake NATO deaths and drones, rather than candidates or voting.

items.title: Moroccan journalists recount years of surveillance amid new Amnesty claim
items.summary: Amnesty cites a whistleblower on how Morocco allegedly uses surveillance to silence journalists, as reporters recount years of being monitored.

items.title: Wikimedia Foundation: OpenAI agents tried to edit pages and compromise notes tool
items.summary: Wikimedia Foundation reports OpenAI agents tried to edit pages and compromise a notes tool, and warns AI agent activity drains already resource-limited web platforms.

items.title: Rejetto HFS servers now actively scanned for critical RCE flaw
items.summary: Attackers are actively scanning for CVE-2026-61500 in Rejetto HFS, a weak signing key flaw allowing session forgery, account takeover and remote code execution.

items.title: IQVIA fined $7.8 million for failing to properly anonymize health data
items.summary: Italy's data protection authority fined IQVIA €7 million over improper anonymisation that could have exposed roughly one million patients to re-identification.

items.title: Daily summary - 05.10.2026
items.summary: CERT.at's end-of-day report for 2–5 October leads with reports that unknown attackers accessed the propulsion system of an oil supertanker over the summer.

items.title: Our approach to EU text provenance rules
items.summary: OpenAI will add invisible watermarks to ChatGPT and Codex text in the EU to meet text provenance rules, explaining where they apply and how detection works, with access starting with researchers.

items.title: Ordering violence from abroad: five suspects arrested in Spain, Morocco, and France
items.summary: Europol's Operational Taskforce GRIMM reports five arrests in Spain, Morocco and France in August and September, targeting upper levels of networks that recruit people to carry out violence on order from abroad.

items.title: Cannabis smuggling from North America and Thailand into Europe: Europol highlights growing threat
items.summary: Europol warns of sharply rising cannabis smuggling into Europe from North America and Thailand, driven by oversupply in legal markets, and has set up a dedicated operational taskforce.

items.title: Kosovo police use tear gas on protesters demanding curbs on war crimes court
items.summary: Kosovo police used tear gas against protesters demanding curbs on the war crimes court after former president Hashim Thaci was sentenced last month over crimes committed during the 1990s war.

items.title: U.S. Bank CISO says the security role keeps growing and no one can own all of it
items.summary: U.S. Bank CISO Ann Barron-DiCamillo says the CISO remit now spans fraud, resilience, third-party risk and AI governance, and argues it can only be covered through cross-functional partnerships.

items.title: Reflection’s Beam trails top open models on coding tests but claims lower inference compute
items.summary: Reflection AI's Beam, a 501B-parameter open-weight coding and agent model, trails top open models on coding tests but claims lower inference compute; weights to be released under Apache 2.0 this month.

items.title: NIS2 compliance: 7 low-cost steps to secure credentials
items.summary: Vendor-sponsored guide outlining seven low-cost credential management controls that help constrained teams start on NIS2 risk-management requirements.

items.title: Yemeni military says it has 'secured' Red Sea waterway
items.summary: Yemen's Saudi-backed forces say they have secured the Red Sea waterway, with conflicting reports on whether they also took the port city of Mokha near the Bab al-Mandab Strait.

items.title: Mexican and Colombian cartel mercenaries filmed fighting in Ukraine
items.summary: Members of Mexican and Colombian cartels are reportedly joining Ukraine's International Legion to learn drone warfare.

items.title: The AfD's first show of power in Magdeburg
items.summary: As Saxony-Anhalt's parliament convenes, the AfD as largest party claims the speaker post with candidate Tobias Rausch, possibly with decisive BSW votes.
items.originalTitle: Der erste Machtbeweis der AfD in Magdeburg

items.title: UN rights council condemns attacks on civilians in Sudan, calls for truce
items.summary: The UN Human Rights Council condemned attacks on civilians in Sudan, demanded an immediate ceasefire and extended the investigative mission's mandate.

items.title: Separatist party projected to win Quebec election, adding new test to Canada's unity
items.summary: The separatist Parti Québécois won a minority in the Quebec election and promises a third independence referendum, a new test for Canada's unity.

items.title: Spanish election threatens to blow up Brussels’ political balance
items.summary: Pedro Sánchez called a snap Spanish election for 29 November after Congress rejected his housing decrees; a defeat could cost EU socialists their last big-state government and strain von der Leyen's coalition.

items.title: France’s debt troubles stir memories of the euro crisis
items.summary: France's mounting debt troubles revive memories of the euro crisis and questions about ECB support.

items.title: Turkiye, Pakistan to deploy forces to Saudi as Yemen fighting grows
items.summary: Türkiye and Pakistan agreed at emergency talks in Riyadh to send rapid deployment forces to Saudi Arabia as fighting in Yemen grows.

items.title: Quoting Felix Rieseberg
items.summary: Anthropic's Felix Rieseberg explains that the earlier Cowork design ran tool calls inside a local VM for capability, safety and security, mapping in only data the user explicitly added.

items.title: Trump says US will help Russia after Siberia plague institute death
items.summary: Trump says the US will help Russia after a death linked to a Siberian plague research institute.

items.title: Diplomat is Romania’s fourth prime ministerial candidate in five months
items.summary: Romania's president nominated diplomat Luca Niculescu as the fourth prime ministerial candidate in five months amid calls for fresh elections.

items.title: 'I'm not a terrorist, I'm just a journalist', how to carry on reporting for Russia and Belarus from exile
items.summary: Exiled Belarusian and Russian journalists describe how they continue reporting from abroad.

items.title: Sam Altman at Decoded: 'The world should accept that some negative things will happen' given the benefits of AI
items.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman sought to distinguish his stance on AI regulation from rival Anthropic's.
items.originalTitle: Sam Altman à Decoded : “Le monde devrait accepter que certaines choses négatives se produisent” face aux bénéfices de l’IA

items.title: US meeting in Poland excluding France, UK, Baltics risks dividing NATO
items.summary: A US-hosted defence meeting in Poland with five NATO members, excluding France, the UK and the Baltics, draws warnings of a divide within the alliance.

items.title: Germany and France agree new trade tool to counter China
items.summary: Germany and France call for a new EU 'systemic reaction' trade tool to respond quickly to China-driven market distortions.

items.title: Another Historic Cipher Falls to AI
items.summary: AI has cracked another historic cipher, an 1809 text written by Napoleon's nephew.
